effect: Pick a level, then a boss run: Zach the Were-Bomberman (instead of Drifty), Partz, Rahtut, Count Dracu-boom and Ms. Flashy, one match each, then the ending
note: Table $27E7E, the row after the four levels. Typed in BizHawk: the level choice comes up, then THE SCARY RUINS with "My name is Zach. I am a Were-Bomberman!"; a normal start (1000) gives Drifty. Tobidase! effect: DEBUG MENU (13 game settings), then a game with them (hold L, R, Up on the right pad and Left on the left pad while pressing A)
note: The last two entries of the button-code list ($27EB6). The check ($0702_00F0) wants pad bits L, R, right-pad Up and left-pad Left; with them held in BizHawk the [ DEBUG MENU ] opens with 13 settings, and A starts a game with them. GameFAQs doesn't have it. Tobidase! Panibon (Japan): typed in BizHawk with L, R, right-pad Up and left-pad Left held, the [ DEBUG MENU ] opens (sub-mode 2).

effect: DEBUG MENU, then a game where the CPU plays both sides (hold L, R, Up on the right pad and Left on the left pad while pressing A)
note: The last two entries of the button-code list ($27EB6). The check ($0702_00F0) wants pad bits L, R, right-pad Up and left-pad Left; with them held in BizHawk the [ DEBUG MENU ] opens with 13 settings, and A starts a game with them; unlike 0825 (this is sub-mode 3, $0700_6D64) your side is CPU-controlled too, so both fields play themselves and the round replays. GameFAQs doesn't have it. Tobidase! Panibon (Japan): typed in BizHawk with L, R, right-pad Up and left-pad Left held, the DEBUG MENU, then a CPU-only game (sub-mode 3).

effect: Your pad moves both sides: the opponent's field follows your Left and Right (hold L and R while entering)
note: Sets $0500_24E8; the opponent's control word becomes 1 instead of $101 ($0700_6DDE), so player 1's pad drives both fields and the CPU never moves. Typed in BizHawk with L and R held: both falling pieces move together. Tobidase! Panibon (Japan): typed in BizHawk with L and R held, sets $0500_24E8.

effect: A RESULT screen after every round: level, chains, giant bombs, stage times (hold L and R while entering)
note: Sets $0500_24E0; after each round the main loop calls the RESULT screen ($0700_7E46) that normally comes only after the ending. Typed in BizHawk with L and R held. Tobidase! Panibon (Japan): typed in BizHawk with L and R held, sets $0500_24E0.

effect: Other block pieces in every game
note: Sets $0500_24F4; a normal game then uses piece set (TUBU) 5 instead of its own ($0700_7C1A). Typed in BizHawk. Tobidase! Panibon (Japan): typed in BizHawk, sets $0500_24F4.

effect: DOKURO blocks in every game: the attack rows you get are brick blocks instead of Bomberman heads (hold L and R while entering)
note: Sets $0500_24E4, which turns DOKURO ($0500_2540) on at every stage start ($0700_7BBA): the 8-block attack row uses block kind $B instead of 6 ($0700_97F2). Clearing one next to a chain releases an item ($0701_2322 -> $0701_5E14). Typed in BizHawk with L and R held, then Normal, The Scary Ruins: the CPU's chains sent brick rows into your field. Image: without the code (left) and with it. Tobidase! Panibon (Japan): typed in BizHawk with L and R held, sets $0500_24E4.

effect: Fewer idle animations in every game: the blocks in the fields blink and wink half as often (hold L and R while entering)
note: Clears $0500_2500, so ANIMATION ($0500_24C4) is 0 instead of 1. $0700_EC68 starts a block's idle animation on a random cell; ANIMATION 0 tries on every 4th frame, 1 on every 2nd, 2 on every frame. Typed in BizHawk with L and R held and counted over 5,000 frames: with the code every start fell on one frame in four, without it on two. Tobidase! Panibon (Japan): typed in BizHawk with L and R held, clears $0500_2500.

effect: Developer menu at power-on: VERSION 1995/07/21 with GAME START, DEBUG GAME PLAY, DEBUG AUTO PLAY, SOUND TEST, ENDING
note: The menu ($0700_0A48) is in the ROM but nothing calls it. The patch calls it from boot mode 0 (file $06B2) and points its three debug items at the sub-mode word the finished game reads ($0500_24F8; they still wrote the old byte $0500_26D9). Patched file in BizHawk: GAME START boots normally, DEBUG GAME PLAY and DEBUG AUTO PLAY give the DEBUG MENU then a game (as 0825 and 0513), SOUND TEST and ENDING open those.

effect: SCROLL, ANIMATION, DOKURO, TUBU, ENEMY, WORLD, SPEED, COLOR, ERASE, ITEM, EVENT, WIN, CPU: the 13 values a stage normally sets for you
note: Left-pad Right and Left change a value. SCROLL background scroll on/off; ANIMATION how often blocks start an idle animation (0 every 4th frame, 1 every 2nd, the normal value, 2 every frame); DOKURO brick attack rows, which drop items when cleared; TUBU piece set 0-5; ENEMY the opponent 0-10; WORLD the background 0-3; SPEED drop speed 0-5; COLOR block kinds 1-5; ERASE blocks in a row to clear 1-6; ITEM n makes every item type n-1 (items come only from DOKURO blocks); EVENT n forces event n-1 and makes a 2-chain enough to start it, for the left player only (a giant spiked robot, rolling explosions, a vortex, a red flood); WIN the round wins that end a match (1, the default, or 2); CPU the opponent's level (0F chains and attacks fast, 00 only clears). All seen in BizHawk (menu $0700_64B0, stage tables from $0702_6588). BizHawk, JP ROM: 0513 typed with L R, right Up, left Left opens the same [ DEBUG MENU ] with the same 13 items and defaults, and the values land in the same RAM (EVENT $0500_26E4, CPU $253C, thresholds $254A/$254C set to 1/2).

effect: A forced event on your first 2-chain: a giant spiked robot, rolling explosions, a vortex, or a red flood that refills the field
note: EVENT n > 0 sets the chain thresholds $254A/$254C to 1 and 2 (normally 4 and 5) and forces event n-1, but only for the left player (struct $5954, whose +8 is 0), so the CPU opponent of 0825 never starts one; with 0513 the left side plays itself. In BizHawk with CPU 0F: each event started on the left side's 2-chain. Image: EVENT 1, 2 (top), 3, 4. BizHawk, JP ROM: EVENT 1 with 0513 and CPU 0F: the giant spiked robot came up in the right field after the left side's 2-chain (EVENT 2-4 not run).

effect: Every item is one type: ITEM n gives type n-1, 16 items in all
note: Items come only from cleared DOKURO brick rows, and their type is normally random & 15 ($0701_5FEC); the effects are a switch at $0701_6632 and work on the owner's field. ITEM 1 bricks become bombs; 2 left and right swapped for about 500 frames; 3 pieces fall at full speed for about 500 frames; 4 blasts use level 0 for about 500 frames (from the code); 5 bombs become rocks; 6 every bomb explodes; 7 the next piece is a giant bomb; 8 a big Bomberman bounces in front of your field; 9 a row of bricks pushed up; 10 four rocks pushed up; 11 STOP: a 5-4-3-2-1 countdown with no pieces falling; 12 bricks drop into the outer columns; 13 the next piece is rocks; 14 every face block cleared; 15 a row of bombs pushed up; 16 every bomb removed. In BizHawk with 0513, DOKURO 1 and CPU 0F: each icon seen, and each effect seen in the field except 2-4 and 16 (seen in RAM). Image: ITEM 1-8 (top) and 9-16. BizHawk, JP ROM: ITEM 7 with DOKURO 1, 0513 and CPU 0F: brick rows dropped items, the giant-bomb NEXT piece came up and blew up as in the US game; the item effect switch ($0701_6632 US) is the same 512 bytes in the JP ROM at $0701_65EE (other item numbers not run).

note: $0701_B1DC follows the sequence on the PANIC BOMBER title (any other new press starts it over) and sets the main mode $0500_26D6 = 6 ($0701_B270), which runs $0701_7E74. Seen together, the bars cross the line: it looks like a chart for lining up the two screens. A or Start goes back to the intro ($0701_7FF2). Entered before the demo starts, seen in MAME (both eyes; image: left eye, right eye) and BizHawk (left eye). Tobidase! Panibon (Japan): the same sequence on its title gives the one-line screen, seen in BizHawk.

code: Hold A, B, L, R, Start and Select during the ending
effect: Skips the ending scenes: the castle door and the statue end at once
note: Mode 7 ($0701_8088) checks the held buttons at each scene's steps ($0701_87EA): with exactly A, B, L, R, Start and Select held (and no d-pad) it ends the scene ($0700_63EE). In BizHawk after a real Doom Castle win: the door scene ended after about 38 frames instead of 525 and the bonus stage began; at the statue, about 37 frames instead of about 966, straight to RESULT. Tobidase! Panibon (Japan), in BizHawk after 0716: with the six buttons held the ending is over within about 600 frames; without them the door and the statue play out.

effect: Tunes and effects the game never plays, some out of the sound test's reach
note: Music goes through $0700_63B8 (table $0707_4024, 00-15) and effects through $0700_63C8 (table $0707_4080, 00-28). Tune 0E and effects 00 and 1F are never requested; only the sound test plays them. Tunes 13-15 and effects 24-28 are past the test's range (BGM 0-12, SE 0-23), so nothing can play them. 0E is a full tune; 13 and 14 two versions of another; 15 a short rising run into a held note, likely a test tone. The effects last 0.2 to 0.8 s. Recorded in MAME. Static, JP ROM: the request routines sit 4 bytes lower ($0700_63B4 / $63C4); its 15 BGM and 79 SE call sites load the same immediate IDs as the US ROM's (same reg-passed sites), the ID tables $0702_64F0 / $64E0 and sound tables $0707_4024 / $4080 are byte-identical, and the sound test keeps the same limits ($12, $23).

effect: An unused set of Star, Sun and Moon medals, drawn rougher than the ones the medal card shows
note: Graphics load through $0700_46A4 from the table at $0704_7000 (LZ, the same scheme as Panic Bomber W). Its 76 call sites name their graphics directly or as base + stage, opponent or world, and none gives $C6 ($0706_6F9D, whose pointer appears only in its table slot). $C6 holds two rows of large star, sun and moon medals in a dithered style unlike the medal card's ($C5), plus a copy of the castle from $C1. Static, JP ROM: the 75 calls of the chars loader ($0700_46A0) give the same IDs and base+index forms as the US ROM's 76, none $C6; $C6's pointer ($0706_713E) appears only in its table slot.

effect: A FLAME UP! message in the LEVEL UP! lettering, never shown
note: Frame $0121 (file $33BEA) sits next to the used LEVEL UP! frame $0120 and uses chars every match loads. Nothing names it: no frame call ($29A4, $3636), none of the 195 frame stores and no code value or ROM table gives $0121. The same picture is in the in-game text sheet (map $21, rows 10-13), but the game only ever shows rows 0-5 of that sheet and copies PAUSE out of it. Static, JP ROM: the frame at file $33BEA is the same; the 74 + 43 calls of the frame routines ($0700_29A0, $3632) load the same immediates as US and none is $0121; the one other $0121 immediate found in the ROM is in data (file $56A2E, the same bytes as US $5685B).

code: Hold L and R after winning a round
effect: The VIRTUAL BOY logo screen, with its corner marks for lining up the display, comes up before the next stage
note: Once WON / LOST is up and about 2.5 seconds have passed, L and R held together set $0500_2444 ($0700_9598) and the game shows its second boot screen ($0701_74B2); A goes on to the next stage card. Real presses in BizHawk: L + R held only earlier, or L or R alone, does nothing. The losing side has the same check ($0700_96B0), not reached. Image: with L + R (top), without (bottom).

effect: A fourth boot screen the game never shows
note: $0701_77FE is built like the three boot screens (precaution text, VIRTUAL BOY logo, OPTION) but nothing calls it. Called in place of the first (file $6BC: 36 6C -> 44 71) in BizHawk, it shows the one line and waits for A. Image: it, then the three screens the game shows.

effect: A recorded demo match the game never plays, and the code that recorded the demos from the pad
note: The demo starter $0700_7014 can replay six recordings but is only asked for five (auto play, 0130); the sixth ($0702_5801, the Sinister Forest, 4,940 frames) plays with file $0A08 C5 -> C6, in place of the fifth. Control mode 2 ($0200 in $0500_595C) is the recorder ($0702_1120), which nothing selects: set during a demo in BizHawk, the pad drove the match and the buttons were written run-length coded to $0500_D0C4, the ROM demos' format. Image: the sixth demo (top); replay against recording (bottom).
